messages:
maria: Heads up — Acme support ticket. Customers hitting 5xx + timeouts to hosted API since ~09:50 UTC. p95 ~= 7.8s, multiple tail timeouts, ticket #6421. Any quick hits?

ops-bot: ALERT: tenant_acme request_queue_saturation detected. queue_depth=324/350 (92%), continuous_batcher.backlog=210, tail_timeouts=152 (10m window).

sanjay: Looking at metrics now — continuous-batcher pending items rising; dequeue rate flat. KV cache miss ratio spiked for acme keys around 09:48.

dbrown: Pulled traces: many long-sequence requests (seq_len ~ 3000-4096). Dequeue latencies show jitter; sample trace id trc_78a9f has dequeue_time_ms=1720 and then a 504.

kevin: Can we reproduce? maria, did Acme provide a repro payload or curl?

maria: They did a replay (approx 200 reqs/min) with large prompts. Example they used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.prod/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"input":"'$(python -c "print('A'*3800)")'","max_tokens":512}'
```

sanjay: Reproduced on staging with traffic-gen. continuous_batcher.window_ms=40 and max_queue_depth=350 => backlog grows and tail timeouts appear. If I lower window_ms to 10ms backlog collapses but small-request p95 rises ~10-15%.

dbrown: Immediate mitigations to consider: reduce continuous_batcher.window_ms for the hosted pool handling acme OR temporarily increase max_queue_depth to 600. Second option buys time but raises memory pressure. Third: route seq_len>2000 to non-batched path / smaller model variant.

liz: @support-team — customer is waiting. Need an ETA/update to Acme in 30m.

support-bot: Ticket RED-6421 created/updated: "Investigating request queue saturation; applying mitigations and will follow up".

kevin: Playbook command for quick change (control plane):
```
# apply small-window to reduce batching tail for tenant acme
kubectl -n inference exec deploy/config-apply -- \ 
  --set tenant=acme \ 
  --set continuous_batcher.window_ms=10 \ 
  && curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/apply-config?tenant=acme
```

sanjay: Ran change on staging: continuous_batcher.window_ms -> 10. queue_depth 320 -> 80 in ~2m. Dequeue throughput back to normal. Applying to prod in 5m.

maria: Applied to prod at 10:12 UTC. Monitoring: queue_depth falling, tail_timeouts down ~90%, 5xx count reduced significantly. Updating Acme. :thumbsup:

dbrown: Follow-ups (post-incident):
- Add runbook step: auto-detect sustained seq_len>2048 spike and temporarily switch tenant to non-batched path.
- Add per-tenant max_queue_depth override and alert when >80% for 5m.
- Investigate why KV-cache miss spike coincided with backlog (possible eviction storm).

kevin: I opened a PR for the runbook + alert rules: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/58 
(contains exact commands, rollback, and customer messaging templates).

maria: Great. Customer updated with mitigation and ETA for RCA. Scheduling postmortem in 48h; tagging SRE/infra/eng-ml.

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: request_queue_saturation for tenant_acme at 7802468315.

kevin: Action items assigned in PR and support ticket. Will follow up on KV-cache root cause.

maria: Thanks everyone — closing Slack thread after postmortem notes added to RED-6421."
